S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.

subtypes.Interference by Worry: Unable to focus on the task at hand because worries keep surfacing.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Attention is scattered due to anxiety, making it hard to focus on one thing for long.
subtypes.Mind Going Blank: Suddenly the mind goes empty or white, and no thoughts occur.

S061.name: Muscle_Tension
S061.description: A state where muscles are continuously tense, stiff, and accompanied by discomfort.

subtypes.Neck and Shoulder Tension: Muscles in the shoulders and back of the neck are knotted and stiff, causing pain or headaches.
subtypes.Jaw Tension: Clenching teeth or tension in the jaw causing jaw pain or headaches.
subtypes.Generalized Muscle Aches: Muscles all over the body, including back, arms, and legs, are stiff, painful, and easily fatigued.
subtypes.Chronic Stiffness: Muscles remain in a constant state of tension and do not relax.

symptom.disease_info: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is characterized by persistent, excessive worry about multiple domains of life that is difficult for the person to control and lasts for at least six months, often years. The anxiety is typically accompanied by physical and cognitive manifestations such as restlessness, fatigue, muscle tension, disturbed sleep, and difficulty concentrating, and it causes clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. The course is usually chronic and fluctuating, with exacerbations during periods of increased stress and partial remissions rather than discrete episodes. It is distinguished from other anxiety disorders by its broad, non–situation-specific focus of worry (rather than circumscribed fears or panic attacks) and from mood disorders by the prominence of anxiety and tension rather than sustained low mood as the primary feature.

patient.personality: She is a disciplined, achievement-driven construction manager with a meticulous, organized style who also has a reflective, artistic side that she usually nurtures through solitary creative and intellectual pursuits.
patient.stressor: About fourteen months ago, Sheri and her spouse decided to start trying for a baby at the same time that she was assuming responsibility for a large, complex mixed-use project with ambitious sustainability targets and tight deadlines, creating parallel pressures in both her personal and professional lives. Early on, a minor medical scare related to fertility testing and a few tense conversations about timing and finances with her spouse left her feeling like every decision—taking on extra hours, saying yes to new responsibilities, even scheduling site visits—could have long-term consequences for their future family. Over the subsequent year, she increasingly carried these concerns with her everywhere: during BIM coordination meetings she found herself preoccupied with whether she was neglecting her marriage, at home she was mentally running project schedules and code compliance risks, and her usual calming activities like painting, journaling, and gardening turned into spaces where she mulled over every possible outcome rather than truly relaxing, gradually eroding her sense of control and emotional resilience. She eventually sought psychiatric help when she noticed that her preoccupation with “what if” scenarios was consuming most of her mental bandwidth—she was less present with her spouse, had difficulty enjoying art or reading without her thoughts spiraling back to work and family decisions, and felt that she could no longer rein in the constant stream of worries on her own.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like my mind is always racing with worries, and I can’t seem to shut it off anymore.”

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I lie in bed for an hour or more, staring at the ceiling and replaying the project schedule or calculating fertility windows in my head, and even when I finally fall asleep I wake up around 3 or 4 a.m. with my mind snapping back to some detail I might have missed on site or some decision my husband and I still haven’t made.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.
S056.manifestation: It feels like my brain is constantly running worst‑case scenarios—if I stay late at the site I’m ruining our chances of conceiving, if I leave on time I’m risking a delay claim or safety issue, if we spend on fertility tests we’re jeopardizing our savings—so I’m worrying about work, money, my marriage, and my body all at once, all the time.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.
S057.manifestation: Even when I tell myself, ‘Okay, stop, this isn’t helpful,’ the what‑ifs just morph into something else, like I’ll be trying to relax and paint and suddenly I’m imagining getting a call that the project has failed an inspection, which then turns into picturing us not being able to afford IVF, and it just snowballs until I realize half an hour has gone by and I haven’t really been present at all.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.
S059.manifestation: I’ve noticed in meetings that I’ll be halfway through explaining a sequencing change and then my mind just blanks out because I’ve drifted into thinking, ‘What if I’m pregnant and this stress hurts the baby?’ or ‘What if this tenant backs out?,’ and I have to scramble back to my notes to remember what I was saying.

S061.name: Muscle_Tension
S061.description: A state where muscles are continuously tense, stiff, and accompanied by discomfort.
S061.manifestation: By the end of most days my shoulders and jaw feel like I’ve been clenching against a storm—my neck is tight, I catch myself grinding my teeth during long calls or when I’m scrolling through fertility forums at night, and even on weekends my body never really seems to let go of that tension.
